process_area.title: Remodel Strategy, Portfolio Planning & Scope Definition

value_stream.name: Store Remodel, Renovation & Lifecycle Refurbishment Program

fields.Participants: VP Store Operations, Real Estate (links to VS-20/VS-97), Merchandising (links to VS-01), Finance/FP&A (links to VS-17.4/VS-40), Strategy (links to VS-33)
fields.Trigger: Annual capital & store-lifecycle planning (links to VS-33.1/W26, VS-40)

Automation Opportunity: - System rule-based auto-approval of "approve the remodel portfolio strategy and roadmap, confirm the capex allocation" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-556 (ensure controlled execution — Remodel Strategy, Portfolio Planning & Scope Definition (PA-109.1).)
- operational: lifecycle scoring (W3474); operational: portfolio governance and phasing
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cadence-misjudgment risk**: Remodeling too late erodes comp sales; too early wastes capital; mitigated by lifecycle scoring (W3474)
- **Capex-conflict risk**: Remodel capex crowds out new-store growth (links to VS-37); mitigated by portfolio governance and phasing
System Touchpoints: - Capex/portfolio (links to VS-40/VS-112); store-lifecycle/asset master (links to VS-35/VS-97); strategy/performance (links to VS-33); merchandising (links to VS-01)

steps.activity: VP Store Operations/Strategy set the store-lifecycle and remodel strategy: target refresh cadence (5–7 yrs by format/age), format tiers (full remodel vs refresh vs re-fixture), category-expansion priorities (links to VS-01.1), market-repositioning rationale, and capex envelope vs the corporate capital plan (links to VS-40/VS-33.1); align to store-growth (links to VS-37) and closure (links to VS-59) plans

Real Estate/FP&A build the multi-year remodel roadmap from the store-lifecycle score (W3474): store age, sales trend, comp gap to market, fixture condition, customer-experience score (links to VS-13/VS-44), and capex affordability; sequence the ~30–40/year program against capacity, seasonality, and cash

COO/CFO approve the remodel portfolio strategy and roadmap, confirm the capex allocation (links to VS-40) and the program governance (links to W3496/W112 PMO), and integrate to the annual plan (links to VS-33.1) and store-operations strategy

fields.Participants: VP Store Operations, Regional Managers (links to VS-07), Real Estate (links to VS-20), Facilities (links to VS-20.3), Merchandising (links to VS-01), FP&A (links to VS-17.4)
fields.Trigger: Annual scoring; store-underperformance alert; age/condition threshold

workflows.name: Store Performance Assessment & Remodel Trigger / Qualification

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Real Estate/Facilities validate physical condition" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "document the qualification decision for governance" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-556 (ensure controlled execution — Remodel Strategy, Portfolio Planning & Scope Definition (PA-109.1).)
- operational: multi-year trend and condition validation; operational: facility survey (links to VS-20)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Score-distortion risk**: One bad year triggers a needless remodel; mitigated by multi-year trend and condition validation
- **Condition-blindspot risk**: Latent structural/MEP defects missed until construction; mitigated by facility survey (links to VS-20.3)
System Touchpoints: - Store-performance/BI (links to VS-28.1/VS-33.2); asset/facility (links to VS-35/VS-20.3); compliance (links to VS-22); customer feedback (links to VS-13/VS-44)

steps.activity: Regional Managers/FP&A score each store on the lifecycle matrix: sales trend & comp vs market (links to VS-33.3), gross-margin & inventory turn (links to VS-101), customer-satisfaction/NPS (links to VS-13), store age & fixture/asset condition (links to VS-35/VS-20.3), maintenance-spend trend, and trade-area growth/competitor pressure

Real Estate/Facilities validate physical condition: roof/structural, MEP/HVAC, floor/walls, fixtures, signage, technology/POS currency (links to VS-99), compliance gaps (links to VS-22/VS-76), and accessibility; flag safety/structural priorities

VP Store Operations qualify stores into tiers (full remodel / refresh / re-fixture / defer) and feed the roadmap (W3473); for full remodels, commission a concept/scope brief (W3475) and business case (W3476); document the qualification decision for governance (W3496)

fields.Participants: Store Design/Concept, Merchandising (links to VS-01), Real Estate (links to VS-20), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Marketing (links to VS-14), Store Manager

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "Store Design/Merchandising define the remodel concept and format" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "Store Design/Real Estate scope the works" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-schedule of "schedule, and Class-3 cost estimate" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-556 (ensure controlled execution — Remodel Strategy, Portfolio Planning & Scope Definition (PA-109.1).)
- operational: clear scope-of-works and change control (W3556); operational: merchandising/market input (links to VS-01/VS-33)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Scope-creep risk**: Undefined concept expands mid-build; mitigated by clear scope-of-works and change control (W3556)
- **Format-misfit risk**: Concept doesn't fit the trade area; mitigated by merchandising/market input (links to VS-01/VS-33.3)
System Touchpoints: - Design/space-planning tools; planogram/space (links to VS-55); merchandising (links to VS-01); capex (links to VS-40); facility (links to VS-20/VS-35)

steps.activity: Store Design/Merchandising define the remodel concept and format: department adjacencies and space reallocation (links to VS-55/W2160), category expansion/contraction (links to VS-01.1), new zones (e.g., appliance gallery, project-design center links to VS-66, solar/renewable bay links to VS-70), customer-flow and queue/checkout layout (links to VS-08), and fixture/finish standard

Store Design/Real Estate scope the works: structural (walls/openings), MEP/HVAC (links to VS-20.3), lighting/electrical, finishes, fixtures/FF&E (W3481), signage/graphics (W3485), technology/POS refresh (W3486), and exterior/storefront; distinguish capital vs expense and phasing (W3480)

Store Design publish the concept brief, scope-of-works, target schedule, and Class-3 cost estimate (W3476); obtain Merchandising/Store Ops/Marketing sign-off and the Store Manager's operational input; proceed to business case

fields.Participants: Real Estate, Finance/FP&A (links to VS-17.4/VS-40), Merchandising (links to VS-01), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Tax (links to VS-79)

workflows.name: Remodel Business Case, Capex Funding & Approval

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-route of "route the capex request per authority" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-schedule of "schedule, and authorize procurement" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: benchmark-based assumptions and post-remodel tracking (W3491); operational: contingency and change control (W3556/W3493)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-optimistic-lift risk**: Projected comp lift not realized; mitigated by benchmark-based assumptions and post-remodel tracking (W3491)
- **Cost-overrun risk**: Remodels exceed budget; mitigated by contingency and change control (W3556/W3493)
System Touchpoints: - Capex (links to VS-40/W1811–W1818); cash forecast (links to VS-18.1); finance/FP&A (links to VS-17.4); PMO (links to VS-112); tax (links to VS-79)

steps.activity: FP&A/Real Estate build the business case: capex (W3481/W3482/W3484/W3485/W3486), lost-sales during construction (W3480 phasing), expected comp-sales lift, margin/turn improvement (links to VS-101), payback/IRR/NPV, residual-value/asset-life extension (links to VS-35), and store-closure-avoidance value

Finance/Treasury structure the funding within the capex plan (links to VS-40/W1814) and cash forecast (links to VS-18.1); route the capex request per authority (links to VS-40/W1813 and VS-36); secure sponsor and executive approval

Real Estate/PMO register the approved project in the capital portfolio (links to VS-40/W1811 and VS-112 PMO), lock the budget and baseline schedule, and authorize procurement (W3481) and construction (W3483) start; track baseline through delivery (W3493)

fields.Participants: Store Design Lead, Merchandising/Space Planning (links to VS-55), Real Estate (links to VS-20), Facilities/MEP (links to VS-20.3), Store Manager

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "Store Design produce the detailed layout drawings" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "Store Design/Facilities coordinate MEP/HVAC/lighting/fire-protection/security/CCTV design" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-issue of "issue for procurement" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-556 (ensure controlled execution — Remodel Strategy, Portfolio Planning & Scope Definition (PA-109.1).)
- operational: clash detection and coordinated design; operational: accessibility review (links to VS-22)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Design-coordination risk**: MEP/structural/fixture conflicts discovered in construction; mitigated by clash detection and coordinated design
- **Accessibility-compliance risk**: Layout fails BP 344 (PH accessibility law); mitigated by accessibility review (links to VS-22)
System Touchpoints: - CAD/space-planning; planogram/space (links to VS-55); facility/MEP (links to VS-20.3); security (links to VS-23); POS/tech (links to VS-08/VS-99); compliance (links to VS-22)

steps.activity: Store Design produce the detailed layout drawings: floor plan with departments/zones, fixture plan and counts, aisle widths and ADA/accessibility compliance, checkout/service-counter layout (links to VS-08/VS-09), receiving/backroom reconfiguration (links to VS-07.3), and lumber-yard/outdoor area (links to W1281)

Store Design/Facilities coordinate MEP/HVAC/lighting/fire-protection/security/CCTV design (links to VS-20.3/VS-23), structural modifications, and technology infrastructure (data/power for POS links to VS-08, RFID/EAS links to VS-23, digital signage links to VS-75); ensure code compliance (links to VS-22)

Store Design produce the FF&E and signage package (fixture specs, finishes, department signage, wayfinding, brand graphics links to VS-14) and the planogram reset set (W3478); issue for procurement (W3481) and construction (W3483)

fields.Participants: Category Manager, Space Planner (links to VS-55), Merchandise Planner (links to VS-101), Store Manager (links to VS-07), Replenishment (links to VS-02)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-file of "Category Manager/Space Planner define the new assortment and space" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "check vs assortment, and the merchandise-reset sequence" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-556 (ensure controlled execution — Remodel Strategy, Portfolio Planning & Scope Definition (PA-109.1).)
- operational: capacity check; operational: clearance planning (links to VS-64)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Space-mismatch risk**: Assortment doesn't fit the new fixtures; mitigated by capacity check
- **Displaced-stock risk**: Clearance of removed SKUs creates write-down; mitigated by clearance planning (links to VS-64)
System Touchpoints: - Assortment/space (links to VS-01.1/VS-55); pricing (links to VS-01.2); replenishment (links to VS-02); merchandise financial (links to VS-101); clearance (links to VS-64)

steps.activity: Category Manager/Space Planner define the new assortment and space allocation per department: SKU adds/deletes/discontinuations (links to VS-01.1), linear/space share (links to VS-55/W2160), category roles, and adjacency/cross-merchandising; align to the trade-area profile (links to VS-33.3/VS-44)

Space Planner produce the new planogram set for the remodel (links to VS-55), fixture capacity check vs assortment, and the merchandise-reset sequence (W3487); Merchandise Planner plan the reset stock and clearance of displaced stock (links to VS-64/VS-05.3)

Category Manager/Store Manager align the reset with pricing (links to VS-01.2/W13), promotions (links to VS-58/VS-14), and labels/signage (W3485); brief the store on the new assortment and train staff (W3490); confirm the reset execution plan (W3487)

fields.Participants: Real Estate, Compliance/Regulatory (links to VS-22), LGU Specialist (links to VS-76), Facilities (links to VS-20.3), Store Manager, Contractor

workflows.name: Remodel Site Survey, Permitting & Regulatory Compliance

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-inspect of "inspections and approvals" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-record of "record for audit" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: early application and LGU relationship (links to VS-76); operational: hazmat survey and abatement plan (links to VS-24)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Permit-delay risk**: Late LGU/BFP approvals slip the schedule; mitigated by early application and LGU relationship (links to VS-76)
- **Hazmat-surprise risk**: Undiscovered asbestos/lead stalls works; mitigated by hazmat survey and abatement plan (links to VS-24.3)
System Touchpoints: - Permits/compliance (links to VS-22.1/W54); LGU (links to VS-76); HSE/hazmat (links to VS-24.3); insurance (links to VS-26); records (links to VS-88); lease/landlord (links to VS-42/VS-97)

steps.activity: Real Estate/Contractor conduct the pre-construction site survey: as-built verification, structural/MEP condition, hazardous-material survey (lead/asbestos in older stores links to VS-24.3), utility capacity, and constraints (tenant/leaseholder consent where BuildRight is lessee links to VS-42; landlord notice links to VS-97)

Compliance/LGU Specialist secure the required permits: building/alteration permit, electrical/plumbing/sanitary permits, fire-safety (BFP links to VS-22), LGU permits per region (links to VS-76), and DENR where hazmat/abatement is needed (links to VS-24.3/VS-73); manage inspections and approvals

Real Estate/Compliance confirm permit completeness, insurance/risk (links to VS-26) and HSE plan (links to VS-24), notify the landlord/LGU and neighbors of works, and release construction to start (W3483); maintain the permit/inspection record for audit (links to VS-88)

fields.Participants: Project Manager (links to VS-112), Store Manager (links to VS-07), Contractor, Merchandising (links to VS-01), HSE (links to VS-24), Finance (links to VS-40)

workflows.name: Remodel Project Plan, Phasing & Live-Operations Continuity

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-schedule of "schedule, phasing strategy" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "Project Manager establish site mobilization, contractor/site HSE" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-556 (ensure controlled execution — Remodel Strategy, Portfolio Planning & Scope Definition (PA-109.1).)
- operational: continuity planning and zone-by-zone execution; operational: integrated planning and milestone management
Pain Points / Risks: - **Trading-disruption risk**: Poor phasing causes excessive lost sales and customer dissatisfaction; mitigated by continuity planning and zone-by-zone execution
- **Schedule-overrun risk**: Critical-path slip defers re-opening and benefits; mitigated by integrated planning and milestone management
System Touchpoints: - PMO/PMIS (links to VS-112); capex (links to VS-40); HSE (links to VS-24); store ops (links to VS-07); POS continuity (links to VS-08)

steps.activity: Project Manager/PMO build the integrated project plan: WBS, schedule, phasing strategy (full-close vs phased/zone-by-zone vs after-hours), works sequence (demolition → structural → MEP → finishes → fixtures → tech → reset), and the critical path; set milestones, budget baseline (links to VS-40/W1814), and risk register (links to VS-112/W3558)

Project Manager/Store Manager design the live-operations continuity plan: trading-area separation, dust/noise/safety barriers (links to VS-24), customer/stock flow, POS availability (links to VS-08), emergency egress, signage for customers, and the lost-sales estimate (W3476); align with Store Ops and Merchandising

Project Manager establish site mobilization, contractor/site HSE (links to VS-24), site coordination, daily/weekly cadence, change control (links to W3556), and reporting (links to VS-112); baseline the plan for performance tracking (W3493) and lessons (W3494)
